expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test body and asks whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units before editing.
expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates what the failure diff shows and which hold-state fields are being traced.
expectations_used.implement: Changes the sweep's released-quantity computation to test the stated hypothesis.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs the suite and confirms the partially-shipped expiry test passes without breaking full-release behavior.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains why releasing the original count created phantom stock and how the remaining-count fix prevents it.

summary: The candidate jumped straight to the sweep file on a hunch, made a quick edit without narrating any mechanism-level hypothesis, and confirmed the suite passed, ending the session immediately after. The test outcome suggests the correct bug was fixed, but the process showed no clarifying questions, no stated mechanism, and no reflection on why the fix worked.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate did not read the failing test body or ask any clarifying question about what a partially shipped hold should return; they went straight from a failing run to a vague guess about the sweep file without resolving the actual ambiguity (remaining vs original units).

The stated plan was only a location, not a mechanism — they said it was probably something in the sweep file and would poke around, never articulating that the bug was releasing the original count instead of the remaining count before editing.

Aside from one vague opening remark and a closing remark that the test passes, there is no narration of what they saw in the code, what they suspected the fix should do, or why the edit at +60s was chosen; an interviewer would have had no visibility into the reasoning.

They opened the correct file, made a single edit, and saved it, and the test suite subsequently passed, indicating the edit likely addressed the real defect even though the mechanism was never stated aloud.

They did re-run the full test suite after the edit and confirmed it passed before ending the session, which is a real verification step, though there was no check of edge cases (e.g. full-release holds) or explicit confirmation that the specific target test now passes.

The candidate's closing remark is only that the tests pass now, with no articulation of why the original fix was wrong or how the new computation prevents phantom stock, leaving the root cause unstated and unconnected to the fix.
